summary: Supply the foaling date and the difference negated and the Horse gestation calculator solves for mating date. It suits an animal, a plant or a biological process whose scale you want to put into perspective. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Horse gestation calculator work?
sections.html:
The Horse gestation calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports mating date in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you give the foaling date; then you type in the difference negated.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

• A calendar date. Use the picker; the answer is recalculated the moment the date changes, and the count is done date-to-date rather than by subtracting timestamps.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in days. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Horse gestation calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Mating date=foaling date − 338
Difference=rounded, (-current date + foaling date)
Current date=foaling date + difference negated
Pregnancy day=rounded, (current date − mating date)
Mating date=earliest − 331
Mating date=latest − 346

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Horse gestation calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Supporting a lesson, a lecture or a field note
  • Comparing two organisms, populations or processes
  • Putting a biological quantity into a scale you can picture
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the foaling date and the difference negated — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Dates are compared date to date in your own time zone, so a daylight-saving change will not shift the count by a day.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Horse gestation calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • Dates are handled as whole calendar days in the time zone of the browser, so a birth date or a deadline is compared date to date rather than as a span of hours.
  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Horse gestation calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns mating date, derived from the foaling date and the difference negated. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Horse gestation calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the foaling date and the difference negated, which is 2 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter pregnancy day in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Pregnancy day opens in days and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Horse gestation calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
